key_insight: Pretraining codec-based avatar models at very large scale (millions of in-the-wild samples) yields striking gains in real-world generalization while retaining high-fidelity control when adapted to studio-quality data.
problem_solved: Bridges the fidelity vs. generalization trade-off in 3D human avatar modeling: enabling high-quality, controllable avatars that generalize from limited studio captures to diverse, real-world appearances and poses.
method: Scale up avatar pretraining using millions of in-the-wild samples to learn robust, generalizable representations.
Use a codec-avatar architecture that compresses appearance and motion into learnable latents, then fine-tune or adapt to multi-view studio data for high-fidelity control of expressions and pose.
Leverage cross-domain training strategies (pretrain on diverse real-world data, adapt on studio captures) to close the domain gap while keeping precise editable controls.
impact: Makes it practical to build realistic, controllable avatars that work well outside studio settings, reducing reliance on expensive multi-view capture and enabling broader deployment in AR/VR, telepresence, and content creation.

paper_title: Large-scale Codec Avatars: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Large-scale Avatar Pretraining
paper_authors: Junxuan Li, Rawal Khirodkar, Chengan He, Zhongshi Jiang, Giljoo Nam
